CLASS IDENTITY FROM ROM RTTI: _ZTS9dCamera_c at arm9 0x02086e6c, _ZTI9dCamera_c at 0x02086ee4, _ZTV9dCamera_c at 0x02086f84 with InitResources/Render/Behavior/CleanupResources/OnPendingDestroy in the inherited fBase_c slots; dCamera_c_classInit (0x0200e444) writes the dBase_c->dView_c->dCamera_c vptr sequence. NOT IN THE RUN: the D1/D0 destructor pair at 0x0200705c stays as its own per-function shards (documented destructor-pair precedent), and the seven handlers at 0x0200af0c..0x0200bec4 stay as shards because func_0200bb28 requires `#pragma opt_common_subs off` and that pragma is TU-global in mwccarm 2004/b56 -- codegen is deferred, so the last spelling in the file wins for every function (the 6ay unscoped-pragma trap). b798/Behavior proved it: they need the default state, so one TU cannot serve both.

the .data claim is the file's own pair of camera workspace vectors: data_02086f20/data_02086f2c are defined, written and read only inside this TU (z written at 0x0200af20-side handlers, x/y read as rotation bases) -- 12-byte Vector3 records at contiguous addresses, bounded by unrelated data_02086f14 below and data_02086f38 above.

notes: Fold of dCamera_c: 16 named members plus 37 camera state handlers/dispatchers recovered as unmangled func_* symbols. mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order, so the file runs ROM-descending from classInit. The recovered bodies were C; each sits under `#pragma cplusplus off` (the pinned -lang c++ build parses those regions as C89, so block-top declarations only) keeping the unmangled symbol names.

Leftovers: the C bodies keep raw-offset member access ((char*)self + 0xNNN) where the real field names are not yet recovered, and the camera state records are TU-local opaque typedefs (CamEntryE, CamFixedTab, CamViewObj, CamStateBase, CamStateIdx, CamJitter, the dBgCh_* shadows). POD `Vec3` shadows replace Vector3 inside the C regions because Vector3's empty destructor makes it non-POD and inflates the stack frame by 8 bytes (measured on func_0200c394).

LOCAL WORKER NOTE: this machine's stock dump is the EU image (gamecode ASMP), so the scratch link built ROM sha256 ddab9300b24aeae254192c2a30d812b07ece3adff83230e75c865ed915c9de40 -- byte-identical to this tree's stock build (matchesStockRom true) -- while the recorded rom.sha256 carries the fleet-canonical stock SHA-256 that every other intact entry on main shares (d1506e90...c478e8). The divergent bytes are NDS container/packaging fields outside every module range; the content proof is identical either way (moduleSetSha256 f9852ffaf80ef19662ab5535df4b13b935188ac3087b5b1d4561c089e4dd802b, symbol inventory and tuRanges all equal the canonical records).

The recorded result is scratch-data-verified: the scratch rewrites are the licensed symbol_binding_rewrites promotions of data_02086f20 and data_02086f2c from STB_LOCAL (file-static) to STB_GLOBAL for DSD's global symbol surface, plus the licensed explicit deadstrip of _ZN7Vector3D1Ev; every other policy was a no-op.

Both globals are spelled `static Vec3` rather than `Vector3` on purpose: Vector3 declares a ctor/dtor for the ROM's dynamic-init globals, which makes it non-aggregate and cannot express a static .data initializer; the file's own POD Vec3 triple emits the retail 12-byte record exactly.
